meta.title: KERI Value System
meta.notes: Generated from the published Google Sheet by scripts/fetch-data.mjs. Nodes come from the Nodes tab; links come from the Vertices tab (Source, Destination, Connection Context, Personas). Only rows with Status "Active" are included. Node weight is derived from the number of connections (3-9); link weight defaults to 1. Weights are subjective and adjustable in the edit panel.

nodes.label: PERPETUAL
nodes.description: Persistent identity, crypto period, pre-rotation, hashed-not-signed, duplicity detection, self-associate data, reputation

nodes.label: ENTROPY
nodes.description: Unbreakable, only bruteforceable, sufficient randomness, uncorrelatable, bulk issuances

nodes.label: SECUFIRST
nodes.description: Security first in the protocol and the system, because you will have nothing if it breaks. Fortify upfront (uncorrelatability), no intermediate infrastructure vulnerabilities, extra security mechanisms where relevant, like decentralization and bulk issuances.

nodes.label: SAFETY
nodes.description: Security first, always, for humans and things, built for fault tolerance and proven context. Accountability so that you have recourse against your peers. Non-repudiation, end-to-end verifiability, verifiable to the root of trust, sign everything, no cross-context correlation. Many eyes make bugs shallow. When in doubt, rotate out.

nodes.label: RECOUPEERS
nodes.description: Recourse on peers: accountability, no exploitation, profiling errors.  You stay in control over peers with profit-seeking motives. Data errors hurt individuals; dangerous, well-meaning bureaucrats associate data without consent. Data can be weaponized against you.

nodes.label: NOSHARSECR
nodes.description: Don't use shared secrets, because you're done (by AI) when you do. No middlemen and no shared governance (blockchain) needed.

nodes.label: MINIMSUFFI
nodes.description: Minimally sufficient (all others will converge to KERI), no partial KERI possible, no "KERI Light", single source of truth.

nodes.label: FAULTTOL
nodes.description: Fault tolerant because you anticipate breaches, theft, errors, etc and you recover from these events, cascade consequences (automatically revoke authorization), no single point of failure

nodes.label: UNBROCHAIN
nodes.description: Unbroken chain of events (2 root of trust, hash tree, blockchain), git and github versioning, actions, versioning and backward compatibility, etc.

nodes.label: ATSCALE
nodes.description: Able to service global scale, omnipresent, any time, anyone, anywhere, versatility, interoperability by design, (be able to) scale up.

nodes.label: GRALIFCONF
nodes.description: Gradual lifting of confidentiality, gradual disclosure depending on counterpart role, contextual display, selective disclosure.

nodes.label: AGNOSTIC
nodes.description: Agnostic; cryptography agnostic, wallet agnostic, intermediate infrastructure agnostic, no vendor lock, versatility

nodes.label: LEGOVPOL
nodes.description: Implementation/infrastructure for Legal (laws, regulations) governance, policies, (readable) Ricardian contracts

nodes.label: SPACTRILL
nodes.description: Spac trillema: Security first always. Gradual lifting of confidentiality. No privacy without accountability, delegated guardian relationships, cooperative, balanced through multi-sig authorizations

nodes.label: ORGID
nodes.description: Organizational Identity and root of trust, first person control and safety, accountability of - and recourse on officers, records of decisions attributable and its context proven, transfer credential sets, legal mandates and obligations, delegation of tasks and responsibilities, you can't have all perks at the same time, verifiable commitments to data,

nodes.label: HARPROB1ST
nodes.description: Solved hard problem first, got rid of complexity, decentralized trust, persistent identifiers, delegable key management, solved problems others can't solve, got rid of username-passwords, truly portable identifiers, made it scalable and faulttolerant at all times

nodes.label: REALMPRAGM
nodes.description: Realism pragmatism: Correlation always on the web, no privacy on the web. Accountable, not trying to constrain; no hiding but 'no exploitation'; simplicity, clarity, availability of tooling, reduce troubles and keep it simple.

nodes.label: CANMODELRW
nodes.description: Can model real-world (authority) structures; all others can't! Asynchronous operation online/offline , sustain reputation

nodes.label: OTHUNSAFE
nodes.description: Other systems are unsafe or insecure, leaking data, being ephemeral, producing false positives, false-negative profiling, etc.

nodes.label: VERCOMTMT
nodes.description: Verifiable Commitments to data, long-term verifiability, non-repudiability, in a cryptographically proven context, wrap and enrich other data formats, verifiable data graph

nodes.label: ANTIFRAUD
nodes.description: The main stickiness factor that's compelling and contagious. Safety is pivotal, but we can't extinguish fraud. Therefore, we need fault tolerance and recourse against bad actors. Because of its decentralized nature, even AI-driven attacks won't pay off. Other systems can't offer this value; they have known flaws that attackers will exploit.

nodes.label: 1PERSCONTR
nodes.description: First-person control embedded in legal structures, self-sovereign identity, no usernames and passwords, create personas, consent through transparency, no phone home; who's the better advocate for you than you? Stop multiple fees for doccing, updating, forwarding, extracting, aggregating data. Not taken hostage by multiple-linked accounts of one company.

nodes.label: ECONINFEA
nodes.description: Economically Infeasible (to attack), decentralized enough, compensate current interests (data harvesters and aggregators)

nodes.label: NOUSEKERI
nodes.description: “Don’t use KERSuite for these things: ”, It's all of KERI or no KERI. KERI makes no sense without Legal embedding, governance structure and policies.

nodes.label: INCLUSIVE
nodes.description: All encompassing, spanning protocol, accessible for all people, most universal, open-source, adhere to open standards, free, if it wasn't open source, we would not consider it. comprehensive utility

nodes.label: VERNOTVAL
nodes.description: Verify do not just validate. Use zero-trust environments, sign everything to be verified, hash data and credentials in verifiable containers, proof and prove. Validation is a manual process, susceptible to human error and randomness. Preempt litigious contentions in nobody's land created by broken validation chains: how to trust the other side of the ecosystem. Less susceptible to fraud.

nodes.label: INCENCOOP
nodes.description: Incentivize cooperation in governance structure, tokonomics, in competition and making money, open and no vendor-lock

nodes.label: PROVCONTXT
nodes.description: Provide and lock in context of the process in a versioned event chain, establish organizational binding and content, schemas, manage personal data/attributes, provably deterministic (no hanging processes/deadlocks)

nodes.label: NOWSTACK
nodes.description: Stack features. “now we can …”, "combinations of the above", etc

nodes.label: EASEOFUSE
nodes.description: interoperability, meet customers where they are, reduce complication, be able to model your solution, hyper churn your credentials, readible streaming formats

nodes.label: BIZEFFCASE
nodes.description: Business and/or efficiency case: Profit, cost reduction, risk reduction, margin higher, but also efficiency: endorsement lifts onboarding and research costs, handling fees to be paid to controllers of your data, single source of truth

nodes.label: INFRASURF
nodes.description: Surf existing infrastructure (OOBIs via X.509, VVP on JWT in Telco, etc), existing laws and regulations, existing programming logic (like structured concurrency in HIO), existing economic models (SEDI), automate manual processes, KERI and ACDC wrappers around existing transactions in existing systems.

nodes.label: GRASPEASY
nodes.description: Easy to explain protocols and tools, simple, clear, as opposed to complicated, not-ingrained concepts, platypus, elephant and blind men

nodes.label: MATURITY
nodes.description: Weathered, complete, thoroughly tested, established in the market, everywhere under the hood, higher-level coding and APIs

nodes.label: COMMUNEDU
nodes.description: Community education of managing secrets, privacy non-existing, selective disclosure, self-association, now being able to stack, (history of) provenance, security breach breaks all, etc.

Commitments and decisions made in a specific role and context are recorded, attributed to actors, and held accountable.

Privacy doesn't exist on the internet, and there's nowhere to hide anymore under the siege of AI. We can't prevent fraud. What we've got left is maximum security and safety through recourse against the exploitation of your data.
Rethinking identity systems should realistically be done at a global scale, long-lasting identifier state, and credentials, and omnipresent.
Simplicity, clarity, availability of tooling, and reduced troubles
Verifiable Commitments to data need to be verifiable in the long run in their historical context.
Any commitment made in a specific context should be proofed (the procedure) and proven (the result positive) and should be verifiable.
We can't extinguish fraud. Therefore, we need 100% sure verifiable attribution to the root-of-trust to enforce fault tolerance and recourse against bad actors.
Fraud committed by known peers in the ecosystem, will be detected, non-repudiable, attributable to them and they can be held accountable as far as legal recourse.
We can't extinguish fraud. But if it's detected quickly and the time window and scope of the effect are small enough, it won't be worth the effort to act maliciously.
Others are susceptible to breach because of known security issues; moreover, they can't prevent exploitation because of the absence of a mechanism for having recourse against bad actors.

Encrypted data is scattered around cyberspace. The decentralized nature of first-person-controlled and state-endorsed identity, fundamental security measures and the fault tolerance in the protocol make it economically infeasible to attack.
Authoritative data structures deliver unbroken chains of events, attributable and authentic in a cryptographically verifiable way.
When there are zero-trust environments, everything is encrypted, signed and hashed to be verified, and there's a procedure to prove in place, then it becomes infeasible to attack.
Cryptographically encapsulated and watermarked content and (meta)data can also be cryptographically verified to the root-of-trust to abide by the security first principle.
A chain of evidence is as strong as its weakest link. To prove context, it needs to be unbroken.
Reuse components that may even enforce each other increases the ease of use as a whole.
The more variations possible of interoperable, securely stacked components, the more ability we have to usefully model the real world.
Because of crypto periods, AI and quantum computing, persistent identifiers need near-perfect entropy as a basis for their cryptography and cryptogrpahical operations.
Persistent identity needs long-lasting security foundations and measures because there's no trade-off: you're either secure or broken.
Security first always, and added to the mix of perpetual safety is first-person control, duplicity detection, fault tolerance, and recourse against exploitation.

Persistent identity has very little trade space with the emergence of AI. It's either a centralised continuous identity system with tracking and surveillance or SEDI/KERISuite-based solutions, all the other solutions are provably unsafe.
Near perfect randomness, very difficult to break, is one of the most foundational features of the security-first-always principle.
Security first always in the protocol and the system, demands near perfect randomness, very difficult to break.
The Security-first-always principle in a protocol and system fully rejects shared-secret-based infrastructure.
Other identifier systems accept one or more known vulnerabilities to which they are susceptible in the AI age. This is unacceptable within the security-first-always  principle.
Other identifier systems are susceptible to known attacks. Moreover, they are not fault-tolerant when broken.  Lastly, they lack the supporting evidence needed to mount a recourse.
Accountability needs attribution, context, and proof. Other systems lack the supporting evidence needed to mount a case for recourse.
Shared-secret-based infrastructure that fully rejects shared-secret-based solutions adheres to the Security-first-always principle of a protocol and system.
Because other systems accept shared secrets in their foundations, they are susceptible to attacks. Those that don't are safer.
Always striving for minimally sufficient means adds to scalability of any infrastructure.
Anticipating breaches, theft, errors, etc by taking precautions and having automation in place to recover from these events, adds to a system's safety.
Fault-tolerant systems are safer than those without that capability.

Other systems break their recorded chain of events for various reasons (signed and expired, trusted middlemen involved, unproven governance, unproven data authenticity, shared secrets, broken backward compatibility, etc.), instantly rendering the chain unverifiable.
General trust in digital services universally operated at a global scale naturally grows to a competence to be inclusive.
Other identifier systems are less safe to use because they have very rigid disclosure mechanisms; you either see all or nothing, always or never, etc.
A variety of possible components supporting a certain task in a protocol makes it less feasible to attack successfully and persistently.
No vendor lock-in and open competition ensure a level playing field, support healthy business models, and improve efficiency in all parts of the protocol where multiple providers can operate.
Rules and regulations need to be set up to incentivize cooperation among actors involved.
No privacy without accountability, delegated guardian relationships, cooperative, and balanced through multi-sig authorizations A combination of cryptography and legal liability is required.
Solved hard problem of persistent identifiers first: truly portable (pre-)rotatable identifiers and credentials that stand the test of time (cryptoperiods)

Designing fault-tolerant protocols and systems is often a hard problem. Examples: decentralized self-sovereign identifiers, rotation of private keys, transferring ownership and control over credentials, and obfuscating content and metadata through bulk issuances.
A hash-graph of data containers, authentically chained together and in a proven context
To keep a protocol working at scale from inception, through growth, and in maturity.
Solved hard problem first to self-address identifiers with authentic authoritative data attached, prove the content and metadata in a blinded state, and selectively and gradually disclose the data.

Can model real-world (authority) structures in a consistent way; all others can't. Think of breached identifiers: no security, then no privacy, and no confidentiality. How to sustain real-world reputation in a system that's susceptible to breaches and has known flaws that attackers will exploit?
We can't extinguish fraud. However, best possible safety against attacks stems from decentralization, fault tolerance and recourse against bad actors.
First-person control embedded in legal structures, secondary roots of trusts, self-sovereign role-based identity.

First-person control over (attestation about) personal data is operated by cryptographic solutions that alone cannot sustainably protect privacy, either individual data rights against surveillance and exploitation. A combination of cryptography and legal liability is required, and that spurs first-person action: Who's the better watchdog for you than you? Stop the exploitation of your data.
First-person control over identifiers, data, and credentials ignites self-sovereign guardianship. And who's a safer guardian than you?
First-person control needs to be embedded in legal structures, governance and policies, such as a fiduciary act.
